title: Collection or Delivery?
prerequisites: Know common days and clock times
objective: Confirm whether a customer order is for collection or delivery, then read back the day and time.
observable_outcome: The learner can correct an order method and confirm the method, day, and time in one readback.

scenario.customer_words: I'd like the cake for collection on Saturday at 11:30.
scenario.problem: The order card shows delivery, but the customer said collection.

model.pattern: Just to confirm, that's [method] on [day] at [time], right?
model.example: Just to confirm, that's collection on Saturday at 11:30, right?
model.grammar: Use that's plus a noun phrase to read back recorded details.
model.meaning: The speaker checks that the recorded method, day, and time match the customer's words.
model.appropriateness: Just to confirm signals a careful check. Right? invites correction without blaming the customer.

options.text: The method: delivery should be collection.
options.feedback: Yes. Saturday and 11:30 match. The method does not.

options.text: The day: Saturday should be Sunday.
options.feedback: No. The customer said Saturday. The card already says Saturday.
No. The customer said 11:30. The card already shows 11:30.

activities.prompt: Which check is clear and useful?

options.text: Just to confirm, that's collection on Saturday at 11:30, right?
options.feedback: Yes. It checks all three details and highlights the corrected method.
It identifies a problem, but it does not confirm the correct method, day, or time.
This is broad. A specific readback asks less work from the customer.

activities.answer: Just to confirm, that's collection on Saturday at 11:30, right?
activities.feedback_correct: Complete. The readback confirms method, day, and time.
activities.feedback_retry: Include the opening, method, day, and time.

transfer_task.situation: A flower customer says: Please deliver the flowers on Tuesday between 2 and 3 p.m.
transfer_task.instruction: Write or say one readback. Confirm the method, day, and time window before opening the self-check.
possible_answers: Just to confirm, that's delivery on Tuesday between 2 and 3 p.m., right?
So, we're delivering the flowers on Tuesday between 2 and 3 p.m. Is that right?

retrieval_prompt: Tomorrow, recall the four parts: check phrase, method, day, and time.

visual.title: The three-detail readback
visual.alt_text: A layered paper-cut path connects a telephone, an order card, three detail labels, and a confirmed collection ticket. The labels are method, day, and time.
visual.text_equivalent: Customer words lead to an order card. Compare method, day, and time. Correct any mismatch. Read all three details back.

scenes.caption: The customer says collection. The card says delivery.
Compare three details: method, day, and time.
